system.name: Mira
system.one_liner: a system that profiles program behavior to automatically configure caching and code for far-memory execution

components.name: Local Node
components.role: the local machine hosting the application and local Mira runtime

components.name: Local DRAM Cache
components.role: local cache split into sections managing different objects/data

components.name: section 1 (fully assoc)
components.role: a fully-associative cache section within the local DRAM cache

components.name: section 2 (set assoc)
components.role: a set-associative cache section within the local DRAM cache

components.name: Default Swap Section
components.role: universal swap section holding all heap objects and static data before profiling-driven specialization

components.name: Application Processes
components.role: the unmodified user program(s) running on the local node

components.name: Network Stacks
components.role: local runtime networking component moving data to/from far memory

components.name: swap sys
components.role: traditional page-swap mechanism used as a fallback path

components.name: Alloc
components.role: local allocator component for cache sections

components.name: Far-Memory Node
components.role: the remote machine providing far memory and offloaded functions

components.name: Offloaded Functions
components.role: compiled code offloaded to run on the far-memory node

components.name: Mira Runtime (remote)
components.role: far-memory-side runtime handling offloaded network and allocation calls

content.key_idea: Mira's runtime splits into a local-node runtime, which manages a multi-section DRAM cache, application processes, and local network/swap/alloc stacks, and a far-memory-node runtime that executes offloaded network and allocator functions, connected over a network/interconnect.
content.reading_order: Top-down: Local Node's DRAM cache and application processes first, then its local network/swap/alloc stack, across the interconnect to the Far-Memory Node's offloaded runtime at the bottom.

summary: This figure shows Mira's run-time architecture, split into a Local Node and a Far-Memory Node connected by a network/interconnect. The Local Node contains a Local DRAM Cache with multiple sections (a fully-associative section, a set-associative section, and a Default Swap Section that initially holds all heap objects and static data), the unmodified Application Processes, and a local Mira runtime with Network Stacks (2-sided/1-sided transfer) and Alloc components alongside a traditional swap-sys fallback. The Far-Memory Node hosts Offloaded Functions and a remote Mira runtime with its own Network and Allocator components. The layout is a compact, tall single-column host-device diagram with square-cornered, dashed, flat-filled boxes in salmon/pink/yellow tones and bold sans-serif labels, distinguishing this runtime-only view from the paper's separate whole-system Figure 1.
summary_zh: 该图展示 Mira 运行时架构：本地节点包含分区的 DRAM 缓存、应用进程及本地网络/交换/分配栈，通过网络互联与远端节点上的 Mira 远程运行时（网络与分配器）连接，实现向远端内存的卸载执行。
notes: The caption is only two words ('Mira Runtime.') and the supplied paragraph describes Mira's overall profiling/compilation flow more than this specific runtime figure's internal wiring, so some box-to-box flows and color usage are inferred from the image layout rather than explicit prose.
